paragraphs.text: BY THE SAME SAINT SOPHRONIUS. Ode. “The one in the furnace of fire.” I have been burned up by pleasures and my sight has grown dark; renew me, O Christ, with the fire of your fear and make the light of salvation shine on me, that I may glorify you forever. Hate the surfeit of the passions and feast on good things during your sojourn here; delight instead in the luxury that comes from fasting, and turn away from the bitterness of pleasures, my lowly soul, and you will live forever. My soul is hardened and I am darkened by the drunkenness of evil deeds, so I never fix my gaze on you, the only God; therefore pity me and enlighten me, and open to me the gates of repentance. Pure one, who made heavenly our earthy and corruptible [?], by your fervent intercession cause to be directed

our petitions and supplications to your God, the God and King of all. “For I am the one who in the sea…” Be sober, keep watch, groan, weep; through fasting, O soul, cast off the whole burden of sin; by fervent repentance escape the fire; and through mourning tear apart the mourning garment of the passions, putting on the divine robe. Let us all draw near through fasting to the mountain [?] of the best deeds, leaving behind the low, earthbound assaults of the pleasures; and entering the dark cloud of holy contemplations we shall see the lovely beauty of Christ alone, mystically deified by divine ascents. Alas! What will become of me, what shall I do, who commit sin and, without conscience, do not tremble before the Master? For this reason I stand condemned before the trial, good and righteous Judge; turn me back and save me, who have provoked you more than all mortals. Untilled earth, who made to spring up the Nourisher of all, who opens his hand and of his good pleasure fills every living thing by divine strength: strengthen with the bread of life our hearts, made slack by the surfeit of our grievous transgressions. “The one who in the bush to Moses [?]…” Put away, O soul, the sleep of dire sloth, and keep eager watch for the divine commandments; the Bridegroom draws near; carry your lamp and hasten to go out to meet him. I have been grievously wounded by the sword of pleasure; heal me, compassionate one, O Word, with the dressing of your merciful favor, so that I may glorify you with thanksgiving unto [?]

From harmful passions, from envy and jealousy, from all wickedness abstain, O soul, and be nourished by the foods that immaterially procure the delight above. Pure Mother of God, heal the wounds of my soul, the passions of my heart and the straying of my mind, since you alone are the helper of sinners and of those who are being ravaged [?]

“Who of the earth-born has heard such a thing?” Who of the earth-born has ever slipped so far and provoked God to anger? Who has followed the impulses of wickedness and been found a lodging place of sin, as I have, wretch that I am? But you, as God who delights in mercy, [?] me

Godlike powers of the angels, entreat God, who is easily reconciled, to save a soul swimming in the sea of worldly cares, storm-tossed by the billows of the passions and endangered by the assaults of the hostile spirits. Come, O soul, made light on the wings of the virtues through fasting, rise above low, earthbound wickedness and delight in the highest contemplations, which procure the delight of good things, now that you have become godlike through faith. Who will make your praises heard, pure one, who beyond understanding bore the one who is praised, the Master and

Lord, whom the ranks of the angelic commanders praise? Entreat him, then, for a people that has sinned, Virgin who knew not wedlock. “The desert has blossomed.” Let us crucify our members through self-control; let us be sober in prayer, as it is written, and let us live in the footsteps of the one who suffered and put the passions to death. Having vomited up bitter sin, let us hasten to please Christ, who willingly tasted gall and by the cross brought down the author of evil. Sin, having become a habit, drags me to utter destruction; but redeem me from it by your cross, compassionate and most merciful one. Lady, since you bore the Master, you hold sway over all created things: set me free from the slavery of the crafty one, our only enemy. “Once a furnace…” A furnace of passions sets my soul ablaze; but quench it with the dew of your mercy, Benefactor, you who, when crucified, poured forth streams of dispassion from your undefiled side through your great condescension. You raised us up when we had fallen into wickedness, O Christ, by being lifted up on the cross; so bring me up, who have slipped into the pits of sin, and establish me, Rock of salvation, that I may glorify your might. With your spear, O Christ, cleanse the rot of the passions from my heart and sanctify wholly the one whom the serpent wounded with venomous teeth; and grant me to walk without hindrance on divine paths. You are the shining lamp and lampstand in which the fire of the Godhead dwelt and gave light to those held fast in night-dark corruption; let us all honor you, undefiled one, and bless your Child, O blessed one. “Of the Father without beginning…” Brighter than the sun, the grace of fasting, rich in light, has shone forth and announces to all the rays of the cross, the beams of the precious passion, and the saving day of the resurrection. Let us long for purity and flee fornication; let us gird our loins with chastity, so that we may appear [?] pure before the Pure One, who alone seeks purity from all, the Savior of our souls. O Christ, nail down my flesh with your fear; you who nailed Adam's sin to the cross, loose the bonds of my evil deeds, shatter the arrows of the Evil One with your spear, Master, and deliver me from the harm he does. Virgin, who bore Christ the Lord, the most righteous Judge and the only one easily reconciled, deliver me, Maiden, from the judgment, the fire and the punishment that the enjoyment of sin has stored up for me. “You who made wise beyond orators [?]…” You who by the preaching made your disciples luminaries to the ends of the earth, Son of God, our hearts

enlighten with the light of the virtues and cleanse by fasting, granting your servants the repentance of conversion, so that they may glorify you, who alone exist, supremely good one. “You have come forth from a Virgin.” Receive the rays of self-control and be illumined, O soul, and flee the gloom of sin, so that the radiance of forgiveness may dawn on you by the divine Spirit. The crafty one baited me with the hook of pleasure and took me captive; but you apostles, who caught the world in the net of the word, redeem me from his wickedness. You were shown to be rays of the Sun of glory, glorious apostles, driving away the mist of error; now enlighten me, who am darkened by every wickedness. I will cry out to you night and day in my affliction, and I will be delivered; I will leap over the wall of pleasures and be saved, walled about by your power, O Virgin. “By the tyrant's decree…” Let us fast from every pleasure, embittering the senses by fasting, and let us fervently drink the draught of compunction, singing: “Bless, you works…” Apostles, when you sit with Christ to judge mortals, entreat that I, who am liable to judgment for many sins, may have a share in the place at the right hand. Purified by fasting, let us mount the chariot of the divine virtues and let our mind fly up to the heights of heaven, singing: “Bless, you works…” You remained unburned, O Virgin, though you bore the fire of the Godhead; but burn up the passions in the souls of those who cry out always: “Bless, you works…” “You who held in your womb God, whom nothing can hold.” Cast into a vast sea of pleasures, I call upon the abyss of your compassion: Save me,

“The illumination of those in darkness.” Seeing the sloth in me, the deceitful one hastens to work together with sin, for he rejoices at my punishment; but you, Savior, grant me correction, to his destruction, I pray. You who on your cross triumphed over the principalities of darkness, rescue me from their villainy, for I have fallen into the depth of sin and into a pit of shameful deeds, yet I hope to be saved by your mercy. You who were put to death stretched out on the cross, give life to my soul, which sin has put to death, and count me worthy, O Christ, to reach your holy resurrection in peace, carefully keeping your ordinances.

Illumination of my weakness, salvation of my darkened soul, pure one, save me, save me who am perishing, Maiden, and clothe me with the garment of incorruption, for I have been corrupted by dreadful transgressions. “The one in the furnace of fire.” You humbled yourself and were lifted up on the cross, raising up in your compassion the one who had fallen by eating from the tree [?]; therefore we hymn you, who alone are praised above all, the glorified one, forever. Through the drowsiness of heedlessness I have sunk into the heavy sleep of sin; but you, my Christ, who slept on the cross for my sake, raise me up, for I have fallen, so that the night of my passions may not overtake me. Blinded by pleasures, I carry about a darkened soul, and the crafty enemy laughs to see me; therefore enlighten me and redeem me from his wickedness, O Christ, forever. I have spent my life in negligence and my soul is weighed down by the drowsiness of sin; but I run to your sleepless intercession: do not let me sleep the sleep of death, all-immaculate Virgin. “The one before the sun…” My soul is leprous with shameful thoughts: cleanse it with the sprinkling of your blood, Word of God, and make me a sharer in your glory, you who for my sake willingly endured the shameful crucifixion. I am bent double under the weight of shameful deeds, Savior, and with downcast face I cry to you, Lover of mankind: heal the incurable wounds of my soul with your precious wound, that I may hymn your Godhead. I make wickedness my food and negligence my drink, and though I remain uncorrected in everything, I take untimely pride in abstaining from foods; but the Lord did not say that fasting would be like this. The abolition of the ancient and severe sentence, the restoration of our first mother, the cause of our race's kinship with God, the bridge to the Creator: you, Theotokos, we magnify. “The mighty captains…” Only good one, fountain of mercy, Lamb of God who as God takes away the offenses of the world, save me, tossed by the billows of sins, and steer me to the harbor of repentance. Pure fasting is the putting away of sin, estrangement from the passions, love for God, diligence in prayer, tears with compunction, and care for the poor, as Christ commanded in the Scriptures. My soul is struck by the sword of sin and covered with the marks of many evils; Physician of our souls, heal me as a benefactor, applying to me the medicines of your holy commandments, Lover of mankind. Undefiled tabernacle, all-holy Virgin, I am grievously defiled by the onslaughts of the passions: cleanse me with the fountain of your mercy, and give me showers of compunction, Lady, to flood the depth of sin. “Redeemer of all…” Traveling through the instability of life, I fell among thoughts that are

robbers, and I am wounded and [?]; Physician of the sick, give me your hand, at the prayers of all your saints. A storm of grievous sin throws my mind into turmoil; as you saved Peter, save me, Jesus, as I sink [?]. “All you works of the Lord, bless the…”

By self-control let us put the passions to death; by fasting let us give the spirit wings toward heaven, and let us cry out with compunction of heart: We have sinned against you, O God; in your compassion forgive us. The Most High, dwelling in your womb, made you wider than the heavens and an invincible protection for those who cry out, O Virgin: “All you works…” “Eve, through the sickness of disobedience…” Let us fast from wrath, you faithful; let us delight in unfeigned love; let us break bread for the poor, fed ourselves by divine grace; and with tears let us quench the tears of the sentence to come. Wretched soul, groan, be downcast, show the marks of repentance; now the day is at the doors, the Judge who judges severely takes his seat, rendering to each what his deeds deserve, as it is written. I have no good deeds; I have stained the garment of divine clothing that I received [?]; I walk in the darkness of ignorance; now, Lord, make the light of your face shine on me in my despair. Mary, Lady of all, I am enslaved by all kinds of sins: set me free, Virgin who bore the Liberator of our souls; for beyond reason you conceived him who took on human nature. “For I am your God.” Groan, weep, O soul, turn back, repent; the hour has drawn near, the Judge is at the doors; prepare your defense and cry out: I have sinned against you, compassionate, merciful, good one; have pity on me. My soul, hate the deadly surfeit of sin; take your delight diligently in the fullness of fasting; make the saving commandments your food, for through faith they procure the enjoyment of eternal good things. Angels, Powers, Principalities, Archangels, Dominions, Thrones, Authorities, Cherubim and Seraphim, beseech God, the Giver of good things, that forgiveness of debts and release from the passions may be granted to us. You alone, all-pure one, bore the Word without beginning, who took flesh from you and was not changed from what he was, and you remained a virgin after giving birth, unwedded one: intercede for us all, that our life may be redeemed from corruption [?]

“The godly-minded youths in the furnace [?]…” You who justified the groaning tax collector and pitied the harlot who wept from her heart, save and pity, O Savior, the souls of those who hymn you. Let us bear the fruit of virtuous deeds through fasting

[?] to the Lord; and let us abstain from harmful thoughts, that we may attain divine delight. The choirs of the angels entreat you, the company of the apostles and the ranks of the martyrs: Jesus, grant forgiveness to your people. The unhewn mountain, the Virgin, the light-bearing lampstand, the ladder easy to climb, the dwelling place of God: let us call her blessed, you faithful. “The one foreshown to the lawgiver on the mountain…” Good fasting, which enriches the heart, makes the ripe ear of the virtues sprout up by divine power; let us long for it in these holy days, as we receive sanctification. Seeing me stained with many sins, wounded and condemned, merciful one, have pity on me in your mercy and save me at the supplications of your saints. Alas, most wretched soul, how will you make your defense? What dread will seize you when the Judge takes his seat with myriads of angels standing by? Hasten, then, and repent before the end. Royal chariot, bright cloud, richest mountain, curdled mountain, unwedded one, I entreat you, O Virgin, heal the passions of my heart. “Let my heart be established.” You spread out your palms on the cross, O supremely good Word of God, abolishing in your tender compassion the sin of Adam's hand, which was stretched out long ago to the tree of knowledge. My mind is shaken by the serpent's envy through the onslaughts of the passions: make it firm by your passion, Lover of mankind, you who suffered and granted dispassion to the faithful. The grace of fasting has shone forth, driving away the darkness of intemperance; behold, now is the acceptable [?] and the day of salvation; let us show the fruits of repentance, and we shall live. Restoration of the fallen, I have tumbled down the precipices of pleasures and fallen into the grievous pits of sin: raise me up, pure one, and guide my steps to life. “The one who in the furnace the hymn-singers…” You who in the abundance of your mercy accepted to be counted among the lawless, blot out my sins [?], that I may glorify you, O Christ, forever. Tear up with your spear the record of my sins, and heal the pains of my heart, O Lord, for it has been struck by the arrow of the wickedness of the evil

[?] child, as it is written; and let us too, you faithful, hasten by fasting to put carnal thoughts to death, that we may attain the life that is there. Alas, my soul, fearful is the tribunal and dreadful the Judge's sentence; hasten, repent. Be reconciled to Christ, who for your sake was hung on the cross and delivered the faithful from condemnation. Open to me the gates of repentance, shut the entrances of my passions, O Christ, you who by your crucifixion made the entrance to paradise easy for the thief, that I may glorify your goodness. I have been cast into the depths of wickedness and am storm-tossed by hostile thoughts, obeying demons and enslaved to pleasures: help me, pure Virgin Mother, and guide me to the way of salvation. “Were you angry [?] with the rivers, O Lord, or was your wrath against the rivers [?], or your onslaught against the sea? Your wrath, or your onslaught against the sea?” Having quenched the drunkenness of soul-destroying pleasures, let us take our fill of the draught of compunction through fasting. Fast, O soul, from intemperate eating; delight in the contemplation of good things, that you may attain the table above. You are coals of immaterial fire: burn up the fuel of my passions, divine apostles of the Savior. You lent Christ flesh from your own: put to death the passions of my flesh, pure Virgin, who conceived Life. “The one who in the flame to the children of the Hebrews…” Put to death by my many sins, I offer up a dead soul in this life; therefore pity me through your life-giving intercessions, you disciples who beheld God, of the [?]

Enveloped in the mist of sin, I have truly drawn near to the hades of despair; therefore enlighten me, you initiates of the Sun of glory, who are his rays and have beheld God. Abstain from the passions, wretched soul, and you will be saved; for abstaining from foods is a fast unacceptable to those who rightly seek it, unless there is also correction of faults

[?] burning with fire, as Moses once beheld you, Virgin Mother of God; therefore quench the furnaces of my passions, snatch me from the fire of Gehenna, and save me. “On Mount Sinai he beheld you.” Apostles, you became rivers from the spiritual fountain and have living water in abundance in a pure heart: dry up the streams of my sin by your prayers and guide me to the way of salvation. A storm of sin buffets my wretched soul; stretch out your right hand to me as to Peter, good Helmsman; let not the depth of despair engulf me, and let me not become food for the soul-destroying sea monster, most merciful Christ. The choir of apostles supplicates you, Jesus, King of all; the ranks of angels entreat you; through the multitude of [your] compassions

[?] correction, and a share in your kingdom. Virginity and childbirth came together beyond nature in you, ark of the holy sanctuary, pure Virgin Mother; therefore I cry to you in faith: sanctify me wholly; redeem me wholly from all the licentiousness of the passions that afflict me. “The ungodly shall not see.” Willingly, Master, you were [?] on the cross, and willingly you dashed the enemy to the ground; so, since I have been dashed down into the pits of pleasures, set me right in your compassion. My soul is darkened by shameful passions: illumine it, Jesus, you who darkened the sun when stretched out on the cross and, O Sun, illumined the whole world and all that fills it. Count me worthy, O Christ, to sail calmly across the sea of the fast, stilling the waves of my mind, and bring me to anchor in the harbor of the resurrection. Let us honor the pure one with a pure mind; adorned with godly deeds, let us piously hymn the beauty of Jacob as the Mother of our God. “The holy children in the furnace…” Nailed to the cross in your compassion, you opened paradise to the thief; now, since I have been robbed by the demon's terrible power and have received in my soul a wound that covers my whole body, heal me, opening to me the gates of repentance in your love for mankind. Let us make the flesh lean by fasting and fatten the soul with prayers; let us feed the poor, purchasing wealth in heaven that is never spent, and crying out: Praise the Lord, you works, and exalt him above all. At your passion creation was shaken, seeing you nailed to the cross, supremely good Savior; therefore I beseech you, compassionate one: my mind is ever shaken by the assaults of the serpent; make it firm on the unbreakable rock of your will. Closed gate of God, through which the Lord alone passed, direct me to divine paths and open to me the gates of salvation, you who are full of God's grace; for I flee to you, O Virgin, the only protection of the human race. “A stone not cut by hands from an unhewn mountain.” The prophet foresaw you, Savior, as a stone cut from a mountain, the Virgin, who split the rocks by your crucifixion; therefore, all-compassionate one, set me free, for I am weighed down by the stone of insensibility. Fast from wickedness, my soul, and delight in divine love; throw the doors wide open to every form of good, and block the entrance of evil through self-control and prayer. Save me, the condemned, Master and Savior, you who by your cross condemned the enmity against me; and do not declare me liable to Gehenna, wounded as I am by passions and darkened by sins.

Spare me, O Christ, when you come with glory to judge the world. Dispel the mist of my passions at the entreaties of her who bore you, and make me an heir of your heavenly kingdom.

“The Hebrew children in the furnace.”

With showers of blood, all-praised ones, you quenched the flame of deceit. Now, by your intercessions with God, redeem us from the fire to come, which is unquenchable forever.

You stopped the mouths of lions and endured the pyre of torments, prize-bearers, and so you inherit the better delight. Pray that we too may attain it forever.

Noble prize-bearers, wholly lit by the light of the Spirit, ask rest for the faithful who have departed, and entrance into paradise, and a share in [?].

I bring you a hymn, O Virgin. Do not overlook me, held fast as I am by evils, but grant me, pure one, a swift amendment through fasting and a good manner of life in every way.

“Victors over the tyrant and the flame by grace.”

In weakness of body you endured every kind of torment, prize-bearers, and you have appeared as physicians to the sick. So I cry out: in the season of the fast, heal my ailing soul through repentance.

Alas! How have all my days passed in negligence? And look, the end is coming, and I am to receive endless evil. Martyrs, who finished the course well, implore that a good end may be mine.

With drops of blood, divine prize-bearers, you quenched the pyre of godlessness. For those who have departed this life, ask the Lord for true divine rest and release from what they have done.

Ezekiel foresaw you, pure one, as the gate through which no one passes, and you open the gates of repentance to all who despair. So I implore you: show me the paths that lead to the places of rest there.

“You passed beyond the bounds of nature … the Creator” [?].

You appeared like divine coals, prize-bearers, burning up the fuel of wicked godlessness and cutting down the hosts of demons with the sword of endurance. You bring light to our hearts.

Noble prize-bearers, you have moved away from the darkness of the mind. So give light to my lowly soul, darkened [?] by offenses.

The all-glorious prize-bearers suffered and endured the pains of the body. Now, immaculate one, they ask for the faithful who have departed a rest free of pain and the enjoyment of paradise.

Appear, immaculate Lady, as a divine helper to your unprofitable servants. In the season of abstinence, bring our prayers to the Lord who reigns through the ages.

“Let us send up a song, O peoples.”

As God you are compassionate. Receive me as I repent, though I squandered my life prodigally. I cry to you: “I have sinned.” I need no accusers, for I bring forward the shame of my own deeds.

I abandoned the food of angels and became like the beasts, feeding on wretched wickedness. But receive me as I return, heavenly Father, as one of your hired servants.

All you faithful, let us leave behind the night of pleasures that comes from luxury and eagerly approach the light of abstinence, so that we may be counted worthy of the light-bearing feast.

Hail, all-holy temple, fleece bedewed by God, sealed fountain of the immortal stream! Guard your flock, Lady, so that no enemy of any kind can besiege it.

“The God-wise children in the furnace.”

I squandered my father’s substance with harlots and was cast out of the courts of grace. But receive me, Father, in your boundless mercy.

Made bright in the radiant fast by the shining light of our prayers, let us become full of light, so that we may escape the darkness of sin.

The choir of the bodiless powers implores you, the Cherubim entreat you, and so do the ranks of the saints: save our souls, O Christ, rich in mercy.

You conceived the cluster of grapes that no one cultivated. I am darkened by the drunkenness of sin: bring me back to a sober mind, Virgin Theotokos, hope of our souls.

“Him who was foreshown to the lawgiver on the mountain.”

Father, I have strayed far from your love and willingly made myself a slave to the urges of pleasure. Receive me as I return, as you received the prodigal, for you alone are rich in mercy.

Wretch that I am, I have turned out a fruitless fig tree, cultivating nothing but wickedness, and it is earning me the fire. So you, Lord, make me fruitful, bearing good deeds as fruit for you.

Fast, my soul, from wickedness and sloth. Master your anger and wrath and every sin, for this is the fast that Jesus, the supreme lover of humankind, desires.

You gave birth beyond all telling to God the Word, who cleanses the sins of the world by the Spirit. Do not cease imploring him for your servants, Theotokos, that we may be saved.

“For I am God.”

The supremely good Father adopted me through the washing of baptism and adorned me with the wealth of every kind of good. But I willingly made myself a slave to fruitless thoughts, and so I became poor.

Be merciful, merciful, merciful to me, Lord! Judge my cause, righteous Judge. Accept my small groaning for the sake of your great mercy, O Christ, and do not overlook me.

Let us strip off the heavy tunic of intemperance and put on the bright robe of abstinence, so that, made radiant, we may reach the radiant resurrection of the Redeemer.

Save me, save me, you who gave birth to the Savior! See my affliction, pure one, which the multitude of my countless evils brings each day upon my [?] soul, out of despair.

“[Him] at whom the angels tremble.”

I lament and wail when I consider the hour in which I shall stand before the dread throne to give an account of my many evils, which I committed both in ignorance and knowingly.

Moses found fasting to be a means of purification, and he beheld God, who alone is pure. My soul, be purified by fasting, so that you may draw near to Christ, the lover of humankind.

Let us long for fasting, the mother of virtues, and loathe luxury, the begetter of passions. Let us cry out: “Our Father in heaven, save us, save us, by the prayers of the

Implore the Judge whom you bore, Virgin Mary, to have pity on me in the hour of judgment, pure one, and to save me, who stand condemned, for you are the only protection of the human race.

“The light-bearing cloud.”

I have fallen into seas of sin, into depths of despair, into tempests of thoughts and storms of passions. I cry out: O abyss of mercy, help me, and in your compassion rain down on me atonement for my sins.

You faithful, let us cleanse the body through fasting, the spirit through abstinence, the soul through tears, and, made pure, let us go out brightly to meet the Pure One, so that we may behold the saving sufferings which the One who cannot suffer endured for us.

Like the publican I groan, like the harlot I weep, like the thief I cry: “Remember me, compassionate one!” Like the blind man I cry to you: “Son of David, open the eyes of my soul, blinded by the wickedness of the crafty

The mountain from which no stone was hewn, the gate through which no one passes, higher than the heavens and all creation, the beauty of Jacob, the all-golden jar, the bridge and Mother of the Creator: let us call the Virgin blessed, O peoples.

“The firmament of those who trust in you.”

Crucified with him who was crucified for us, let us put to death all the members of the flesh in fasts and prayers and supplications.

By your crucifixion, Lord, you uprooted the thorn of sin: uproot the thorny thoughts of my mind.

Having armed our minds with fasting, let us rout the alien hosts of demons, walled about by the power of the cross.

The Word came forth taking a body from you, immaculate one, and in his tender compassion he raised up our forefathers from their fall.

“United to unbearable fire.”

By the cross, Giver of light, you triumphed over the principalities and the powers of darkness. When you come with authority to judge the whole world, do not make a public show of my secrets, O Word, so that I may glorify your great compassion.

You, the Judge, were judged. You stood before tribunals and by your cross condemned the enmity, long-suffering, righteous Judge. So deliver from eternal condemnation those who cry out in fear: “We exalt you above all, O Christ, forever.”

The pious youths, steeled by the fire of fasting, truly quenched with divine dew the flame raised up of old. Let us too, by fasting, put out the furnaces of all the passions, so that we may escape the [?] of Gehenna.

From you, Maiden who knew no wedlock, the Wisdom of God built herself a house and took flesh by an ineffable condescension. For you alone were chosen out of all generations, incorrupt, as a dwelling for the incorruptible Word.

“In the shadow and the letter of the law let us behold the type.”

Moses, lifting up the serpent on the wood, prefigured you, O Christ, who willingly [?] on the cross, beat back the venomous wickedness of the evil one, and drew mortals up to yourself, lover of humankind.

[?] cleanse me with your fear, kindling your divine love in my soul and walling me about with your cross. For the ancient heel-catcher deceived me by guile and darkened my mind with pleasures, O Christ.

Let us fast, brethren, from shameful thoughts and base deeds. Let us purify the heart, take wing with divine virtues, and turn aside from the urges of groveling wickedness, so that, clothed in light, we may behold the great Pascha.

From you, Virgin, the One who is rich by nature willingly put on our poverty. He who is hymned invisibly by the choirs above became visible to us, and in his goodness he refashioned the shattered image.

“Christ is my power, God and Lord.”

Let us show forth fasting, tears, prayers, compassion, a disposition quick to compunction, right judgment and purity of life, you faithful, so that we may enjoy glory.

You appeared in splendor, apostles, shining as luminaries in the firmament of the [?] Church. So give light to our hearts by the divine Spirit.

As divine coals kindled by the [?], burn up the fuel of passion in our hearts, wise apostles of our God.

Unquenchable lampstand, all-radiant bridal chamber, higher than the Seraphim, chariot of the Cherubim, all-blameless one: free me from grievous sins and dangers.

“Out of the flame for the holy ones.”

Fasting made Moses one who saw God, and it took up Elijah in a fiery chariot. Hasten to abstain from harmful thoughts, so that [?] of groveling [?] may not sink the soul [?].

[?] I keep stretching out toward worse things and keep adding wound to bruise. Heal my stony hardness, O Christ, through the mediation of the apostles, compassionate one.

[?] Luminaries of the world, most divinely radiant, scatter the clouds of our passions and make us worshippers of the bright resurrection, singing hymns to the Sun of glory.

Generation after generation calls you blessed, O blessed by God, as you prophesied of old. For you alone bore for mortals the blessed Word, [?] embodied from you

O Lady higher than all, make him who glorifies you as truly Mother of God, and who praises your Offspring, spotless one, known in incomprehensibility, O you favored by God, to rise higher than the wickedness of the passions.
