By their supplications grant enlightenment and the forgiveness of sins to all of us. How beautiful is the season of self-control that you have given us, O Lord! In it have pity on our souls, as you are good, by the prayers of the holy athletes, who [?] your beautiful and holy sufferings. Bring your servants, who have passed through the painful surge of life, into the harbor of life, O Master, to cry with all the elect: Blessed are you, O God.

Ever-Virgin, you who bore the Giver of the Law, entreat him to take away the transgressions of all who, in this time of the present divine fast, have rightly chosen to practise it with zeal. “Dew for the holy ones from the flame.” The heavenly minds marvelled exceedingly at the achievements of the holy martyrs; by their prayers, Master, make your mercies richly wonderful among us.

Supremely good Saviour, by the intercessions of the all-holy martyrs, count the Orthodox who have departed from among us worthy of the life in heaven and of holy splendour. Compassionate One, by the supplications of her who bore you and of your holy martyrs and apostles, enlighten our souls to glorify you in gladness of soul unto the [?]

…for human beings to see God is impossible. The grace of the fast shines like light and urges the sensible to do the works of light. Let us strive to be enlightened in it, so that we may see the light-bearing passion of him who by his sufferings undid the dark passions of Adam. Rising plainly like the sun, the martyrs lit up the whole earth with rays of godliness and lamps of miracles, and wiped out the darkness of polytheism; by their supplications, O God, have mercy on us. Lord, let your goodness reach those of us who have departed at your awesome command; let your mercy surround them and guide them to the dwellings lit by the light of your face. At an angel's voice you ineffably conceived the Angel of the [?] Counsel. Receive, then, the voices of your servants, which we offer in the time of the fast, and offer them to God as [?]

“A song of victory.” Let us put the passions to death through self-control and bring the spirit to life through godly deeds, so that with a most pure mind we may see the venerable passion of Christ. Most compassionate Christ, I have copied the ways of the merciless rich man; I beseech you, number me with poor Lazarus, redeeming me from the flame and the unquenchable [?]. I have fasted from good deeds, and I have enjoyed my sins to the full, Lord; now, then, fill me in my hunger with saving and venerable food. All-pure Lady, you who gave birth to the all-compassionate God, save me and have pity on me, who am condemned and under sentence, cast down by my own works. “Him at whom angels tremble.” Wretch that I am, I have grown rich in fruitless thoughts; I have defiled my soul with lawless pleasures, and darkness surrounds me.

As of old you enlightened the man blind from birth, [enlighten?] [?] my soul, merciful One. It does not see your light, but is buried in the darkness of dreadful forgetfulness and the cares of life. By fasting Elijah opened heaven and watered the thirsty earth with rain; let us fast, drenched in streams of tears from the soul, so that we may [find mercy?] [?]. Virgin, like a living vine you [?] for us the ripe cluster, which poured out for mortals the wine of forgiveness and dried up the ever-flowing [?] spring of sin. [?] I am held fast in the tomb of negligence, with [the stone?] of despair laid upon me. Lift it away, Christ, in your mercy, and raise me up as you did Lazarus [?]. Let us flee from imitating the [rich man?] [?], lest we be condemned to the unquenchable flame, and let us [?] Lazarus [?] in toils [?], so that Abraham may [receive?] us in his bosom when we depart. [?] in fasting [?] let us persistently [?] weep and mourn, [?] fervently, so that Jesus may comfort us and make us sharers in the kingdom. The divine treasure of virginity, the [?] restoration of the forefathers, the spring [?], the [?] of Jacob, the Theotokos: let us who have been saved through her praise her in hymns. [?] the manna [?]. Christ, rich by nature, you who fill every living thing hungered when you fasted; so make me, who hunger for your grace, a partaker of your [?] table. Fasting once steeled the youths in Babylon and made them stronger than the fire; emulate it, my soul, do not [?], and you will quench the fire of the pleasures with the dew of the Spirit. [?] show me poor [?] sin [?], and [?] the wealth which I wickedly [?] of my countless offences, merciful One, and give me [?] thought, for you are good. Rejoice, you who received joy [?], Virgin Theotokos full of grace; implore God [?] that those who sing your praise may be redeemed from dangers [?]
[?] Bearing in mind your judgement seat and the spotlessness of [?], most just Judge, I condemn myself before the judgement; for I fear and tremble [?]

From you, Virgin graced by God, Christ, the Giver of light and peace, rose upon those held fast in a night of terrors. He undid the transgression that came from heedlessness and plainly granted us redemption. “My mind, which has grown barren.” Lord, by the power of the cross strengthen my mind, which grows weak under evil assaults, and direct it toward your will. Christ, raise me up as I sleep on the bed of pleasures in the drowsiness of sloth, and make me a worshipper of your passion. Our souls made bright by the fast, let us hasten, pure, to meet Christ as he comes in the flesh to Jerusalem. Put to death in soul by the malice of the enemy, I lie in the tomb of great negligence; but hasten, Christ, to raise me up. Pure one, who were not burned by the fire of the Godhead, burn up the material impulses of my [?]; always, Maiden, I glorify you. “Him who to Moses in the bush.” Christ, life of all, roll away from my humble soul the heaviest stone of dreadful sloth, and raise me from the tomb of insensibility. Christ, you come again to Judea, which seeks to destroy you, the tree of life, by means of a tree, for you long to make immortal those who were put to death by eating from a tree. Out of compassionate mercy, as God who knows beforehand, you foretold to your friends the death of your friend, whom you were to raise from the tomb on the fourth day for your glorification. In you, pure Virgin, the ways of God have truly been seen: he kept your purity plainly sealed after childbirth, for all [?]

[?] hymn [?] such [?]. By fasting Daniel [stopped?] the mouths of the beasts; emulate him, my soul, [?] the roaring [?]. [?] Word of God, my soul [?] by my sins and shut up in the tomb of transgression: raise it up by your life-giving word and count it worthy to offer you [palms?] of virtues, as to the victor over death. He who holds heaven as his throne and the earth as his footstool, the Word of God the Father, rides on a colt and enters the holy city, to bring forth from the mouths of infants delightful praise as King of all. Among women you alone were [made beautiful?] [?], most wondrous pure one, for you gave birth to the most beautiful Word, who appeared beautiful beyond all mortals. Implore him, then, Virgin, to make beautiful the ugliness of the heart [?]

“Having pondered your divine self-emptying.” Light-bearing apostles, with the rays of your intercession enlighten those who dwell in the shadow of sins and devoutly sing your praise. Faithful ones, joining [love?] to compassion, let us hasten to send them up as supplication to Christ, so that he may raise us from the tomb of our hidden passions. Let us who are dead in soul have no regard for fleshly affection, and let us become dear to the Redeemer, so that he may redeem us from the dread judgement of Hades. Christ, you foretold that Lazarus had fallen asleep; you would raise him shortly afterwards, and then receive the praise of nursing infants carrying branches, tokens of your divine passion. [?] of life, all-blameless Mother of God; those who taste of it, pure one, will be delivered from deadly thirst. “To you, the Maker of all.” God-proclaiming apostles of the Lord, who were shown to be stones of the cornerstone, intercede with the all-compassionate One to lift the heavy stone from my heart. “Let us go,” you cried to your friends, “my friend Lazarus has already fallen asleep. By raising him I shall crush the deadly malice of death for[ever].”

Having become meek in soul and humble in mind by grace, let us welcome the meek Master of all as he comes, crushing the arrogance of the evil one. Enlightened, the prophet sees you as a gate of light, all-blameless one; for you ineffably give birth to [?], made like us, whom we exalt above all unto all the [?]

[?] my mind, which has melted away in the heat of sin, and kindle the extinguished lamp of my heart. “Gate of light.” “The earth and all that is in it.” Women, you who have the Resurrection and the Life [?], why do you lament so bitterly? He is coming and [?] his true friend, the only Benefactor, foreshowing by his raising the rising of all. [?], be opened! Like rational lambs, go out bearing branches to meet Christ the chief Shepherd. The Lord comes forth willingly, like a lamb, to be slaughtered, so that he may destroy the tyranny of the wolf. As you were coming to Bethphage, hostile Hades heard the sound of your feet and clung to the feet of Lazarus, saying: “If [?] is about to call you, do not delay, but come out; for I know that it means my destruction.”

The sacred voices of the prophets proclaim you symbolically as the gate [?]; [?] for those sitting in darkness and shadow the sun has risen, Virgin, the only [?]. “For he has done great things for me.” “Behold,” you cried out, Jesus, “we are going up to [?]

the holy city, and I shall be handed over [?] into the hands of murderers, to be put to death in the flesh on a cross.” Wishing to snatch your friend from death, [?], you willingly hasten to be put to death in the flesh for our sake, making mortals immortal, only [?]. Let us wave palms of self-control before Christ, who rides humbly on a colt in the flesh, and let us say to him as he goes to his passion: “Blessed are you who have come, Saviour.” Awesome is your childbearing, Theotokos, Mother of Christ; therefore all generations faithfully call you blessed, glorifying you, pure one, unto the ages. Amen. “The furnace sevenfold.” “Then you will be known as mine, disciples,” you said, Saviour, “when you become fulfillers of my commandments, as I have told you.” So you came willingly to the venerable passion, through which everyone will obtain freedom from passion, crying out: “Priests, [?]”

“Carrying true humility within yourselves, imitate me, the God who humbled himself,” you said to your friends, Christ, as you went to your divine passion. “Whoever, then, wishes to become exalted and first, let him in his intention be servant of all, crying out: ‘People, exalt Christ above all unto all the ages.’” Let us cleanse the filth of the passions from body and soul, and hasten to follow the Pure One, Christ, who hastens to his passion and grants freedom from passion to all mortals, and to whom all creation sings: “Youths, bless…” Without birth pangs, [?] Lady, you bore him who rescued Eve from the pains she had brought on herself when she was beguiled by the pleasure of eating. Seeing him come willingly to the blessed passion, you grieve and sing: “People, [exalt] Christ,” and so on. “Heaven was amazed at this.” When the brothers saw Joseph, their kin on their father's side, arriving, in dreadful envy they threw him into a pit and sold him far away. He bore the image of the passion of the passionless Christ the King, whom a disciple is getting ready to sell by treachery. Creator of hours and days, you told your disciples beforehand that you did not know the day of the consummation of the whole world, setting for us boundaries of [humility?] [?]. Lifted up by it, through your might we bring low the arrogance of the deceiver. Let us crucify our members through true self-control, crucified with Christ; let us flee the oppressive weight of pleasures and become fulfillers of the divine commandments of the Saviour, so that on the coming day of judgement we may be delivered from condemnation. The fig tree of sin which you once cursed, [?], showing its barrenness [?]. “In the deep he once laid low.” Come, let us gather and all go up today with Christ to the Mount of Olives, and there we shall hear what he says to those who have loved him, as he teaches them about his second coming. With the oil of good works let us all make ready our

lamps of the soul; for the Bridegroom will suddenly [arrive?]. Let us not be found unready, knocking at the door in vain and not counted worthy of compassion. Your disciples go before you, Word of God, seeing you hasten to your voluntary passion. Treacherous Judas is making ready to betray you to the lawless; snatch us all away from his madness and hardness of heart. Maiden Lady, you see the Son and Word of the Father, whom you clothed in a body from your pure blood, hastening to the passion he was pleased to endure in his compassion, and you are wounded, [?] his long-suffering [?]

“Come, peoples, let us sing.” The wicked council has just assembled and is plotting wicked things: to put you to death, Christ, the life of all, with Judas as its accomplice. The house of the leper of old has become a mercy seat, since it held the Propitiation of all; finding him there, the harlot obtains release from countless debts. The wretched Judas, failing to keep your laws, perished through love of money; he plans to betray you to murderers, receiving the noose as his reward. How is it that you come to suffer for us, supremely good One? How do you endure standing before Pilate's judgement seat as one about to be judged? Immeasurable is the wealth of your compassion. The sayings of the God-proclaimers that were sung of old about you, immaculate Virgin, have been fulfilled; for you bore the Word in the flesh, who willingly accepted suffering. “In the deep he once laid low.” Now, with the cymbals of David, let us sing a victory hymn to the Redeemer in thanksgiving; for he has overcome death, granting redemption and life, as the Lover of mankind, to those who had been fettered from the beginning of time. Seen among the dead with your soul, Christ, having accepted a voluntary death in the flesh, you set souls free, raised them with you and made them shine with light, only Giver of life, venerable and purifying Pascha. The Lamb sacrificed for us, the saving Pascha, has come back to life from the dead today and has taken Hades captive, removing those it had swallowed as prisoners, who cry: “Great is your might, only Redeemer!” Unwedded, all-holy Bride of God, the glorified Lord, who showed you to be a pure virgin even after childbirth, has risen from the dead on the third day and gladdened creation; for he has been gloriously glorified. “The desert has blossomed like a lily, Lord.” By your descent beneath the earth, Lord, you led out in strength those who were fettered, and by your death you put to death the arrogant serpent who provoked you. This is the day which the compassionate Lord has made; rejoicing in spirit and heart, let us be glad and dance in it. Redeemed from the tyranny of the persecutor by the blood of the pure and spotless victim, let us now hold festival, shouting in praise. The Lord, shining forth from the tomb, offers you the “Rejoice”;

for it befits you alone, immaculate one, full of grace, who did away with the grief of Eve. “You have come from a Virgin.” Seeing you rise from the tomb as a sun that never sets, the disciples, like bright-shining stars, lit up the whole world under the sun with the radiance of their preaching. Let us hold festival in spirit and dance: the Lord has risen, the divine Pascha, granting joyful grace to those who worship his condescension. Announcing your venerable resurrection to your friends, Master, the women said this with great joy: “We have seen the Lord, and we were the first to receive his ‘Rejoice.’” The most holy choir of myrrh-bearing women rejoices with you, all-blameless one, as it beholds the Word risen, whom you bore beyond cause and reason. “The Giver of light.” The Giver of light went beneath the earth with his soul, led out the prisoners there, and rose in power, granting immortality to the faithful. Yesterday, Lord, I died with you, who died for me; but today I am brought to life with you, for I have you as true life and as the Pascha that cleanses the soul. Leaning on the cross as on a staff and supported by it, let us eat the pure Pascha, driving from our minds the bitter herbs of the pleasures of the flesh. Queen of all, who gave birth to the King of all, rejoice and dance as you see him come forth, beautiful, from the tomb, as from the bridal chamber of your womb. “Encircled in the abyss of offences.” It is the radiant day of the resurrection; let us all become radiant in soul. The Redeemer has risen, having emptied the kingdom of Hades. The company of holy women, seeing the Life risen from the dead, rejoiced with the disciples and celebrated the divine Pascha. The tears of grief have ceased; for Jesus, the giver of joy, has risen and in his compassion has raised with him the whole substance of mortals. You did not open the gates of virginity, nor did you break the seals of the tomb, Master, when you rose on the third day, working all things by your will. “The ungodly decree.” The deadly persecutor has vanished; the lightless kingdom of Hades has been emptied. For Christ, the timeless and imperishable light, has flashed forth; he has risen, filling the world with joy today. All-glorious, supremely good One, when your side and hands were pierced you poured out for me streams of immortality; by death, Saviour, you put death to death, and by your rising you raised the dead with you. To the myrrh-bearing women as they wept [?], Christ [said?]: “I have risen; cast away your lament; tell my friends to come and meet me and to cry aloud the victory song to my might.” [Having kept you a virgin?] after childbirth, he who works all things

by the divine will was seen as a man, God-graced one, granting resurrection to all, as Benefactor and all-glorious. “Him who in the furnace of fire.” Jesus, you appeared as a radiant and beautiful bridegroom, as from a bridal chamber, renewing incorruption for us through the tomb; you struck the guards as if dead, and gave life to those who believed in you, the Giver of life. “Be made immortal by my death,” you cried to your friends, “and proclaim the great Pascha greatly and radiantly to the families of the nations, so that all may know me, Christ, the victor.” “You will live in me, beloved disciples; for I, who am life, have risen in glory, as you see,” you cried. “Sound the trumpet in gladness of soul unto the ages.” The Virgin, beholding her Son risen from the dead, cried: “You have been made beautiful, my life-giving Son, having put death to death by death; therefore all creation glorifies you with one voice.” “The Word, God from God.” Made like human beings in all things except sin, Jesus, King of all, you die and lie in a tomb; but you rise without sharing in corruption, renewing for the faithful the ways into incorruption by your divine resurrection.

This is our day, which the Lord has truly made, doing glorious and ineffable things in it. Let us be glad in it and cry with a loud voice: “You were sacrificed, Lord, as our revered Pascha.” [?] “Why do you seek the precious myrrh with myrrh? He has taken away the stench of Hades, breathed release upon the prisoners, and risen in glory. Be filled with joy,” cried the angel flashing like lightning at the tomb to the women. With the myrrh-bearing women and the wise apostles, all-blameless one, seeing your Son and God risen from the dead as he said, take up festal joy, imploring unceasingly that our souls be saved. “He who of old [?] the waters.” He who of old hung the earth upon the waters hangs willingly on the tree; from his side gushes the water of forgiveness, and in his compassion he dries up the wickedness that springs up through transgression, for he has been glorified. Lifted up from earth to the things above on the most radiant day of Pascha, and forming choirs in it today, let us send up praise to the slayer of death, our only King, for he has been glorified. “Women, why do you seek the priceless myrrh with myrrh?” the angel who appeared at the tomb cried radiantly. “Go, proclaim to the disciples: he has risen and filled the ends of the earth with fragrance.” Immaculate Virgin, seeing your Son risen from the tomb, beautiful in his loveliness, you rejoiced radiantly with the disciples; therefore we cry to you: “Cause of joy, rejoice; [?] finding, manifestation of life.” “My people, for [?] I am Lord of the dead and the living.”

[?] crying out: Save us, O Savior, you who saved Israel from bondage. [?] When the lawless saw the veil torn at your crucifixion, [?] were split, as it is written; and, not pierced with compunction, they offered you vinegar mixed with gall to drink. My sin you [?] when you were nailed to the tree, O Lord; and falling asleep in the tomb as one dead, you raised those who slept from their tombs to see the light of your resurrection, O life-giving Savior. O great and venerable Pascha, through which we were delivered from corruption, from the darkness of pleasures, and from bondage to bitter Pharaoh! Son and Word of God, grant us to delight in your kingdom. Christ, who was born of your pure blood, O ever-Virgin, who was crucified in the flesh and buried, and who gave life to those long buried — by your motherly boldness make him gracious to us. He who brought all things out of nothing… O Sun of glory, invisible King, when the sun saw you hanging it drew in its light, the earth quaked, and creation trembled in fear of you. Today Christ the Lord was seen in beauty, coming forth from the tomb as from a bridal chamber, and he bestows on us the beauty of divine [?]. Christ is the great and holy Pascha of the Lord; for from the tomb you have been set free today from the bonds of sin, as you sing the praises of the destroyer of Hades. Him who was crucified and buried and, as he had foretold, raised from the dead on the third day, O Mother of God, implore [?] to save your servants, O Virgin. You set toward us… You, the Judge, stood before the judgment seat of Pilate, bearing spitting and blows; and going down into Hades you struck its kingdom, raising up those it had swallowed long ago. Pascha is the radiant feast of feasts and the festival of all festivals, O faithful; let us cry to the victor over Hades: You have worked wonders in giving us life; glory to your [?]
The choir of disciples rejoices [?] the Teacher, who truly cast down death by death, emptied the palaces of Hades, and rose from the tomb, as [?]

On earth you, the invisible one, were seen [?]. Having fallen asleep willingly on the cross, you went down with your soul among those who sleep unwillingly among the dead, O Lover of mankind, and mightily raised them up with you. "Do not seek the living among the dead; do not [?] with weeping to see the consolation of all," the angel flashing like lightning declared to the myrrh-bearers. The company of the disciples, seeing you shine forth from the dead,

O Word, was filled with joy, and in the Spirit celebrates the divine and saving Pascha with clapping. The Word, whom you supernaturally made flesh from your all-holy blood, you beheld risen from the dead on the third day, O Virgin Mother. The uttermost abyss of sins… Sing and chant to God, who by his passion overthrew the enemy of all; keep festival, peoples, tribes and tongues of the earth, and clap your hands: The Lord has risen! The enemy has been wounded by your spear, and the flaming sword turns its back to those who [?] proclaim your resurrection and sing your praises, O Jesus, supremely good. Today we truly celebrate the very rising of the Master of creation; for in it he raised the world together with himself, and, being put to death, he put to death the [?]

All-pure one, who alone mediated beyond understanding between the Creator and mankind, implore your Son to show himself merciful to your servants who have sinned, and to be their champion. The youths in the furnace… Clap your hands today, you nations, as the psalm says: Christ has risen, raising with him the dead, who cry with a loud voice: Blessed are you, the God of our fathers. [?] the feast of Pascha, and let us cry aloud: You who have done great things for our redemption, blessed are you,

Women, come from the sight today, as Scripture says, and announce to Zion the good news of the rising of him who was born of the Virgin and loosed Eve from her bitter pangs. [?] O light-bearing cloud, the great Sun who beyond reason dwelt in your womb, O Virgin, Christ, dawning from the tomb, has illumined all the earth with divine rays

"Go out into all the nations," the Master cried to the apostles, "proclaiming my awesome rising from the tomb and the truly complete overthrow of Hades, and that I reign over the dead and the living." "Rejoice," you cry to your myrrh-bearers, who embraced [?] the holy feet whose sound our first mother once feared; and you make them bearers of good news to the apostles, saying: "The Lord is risen, and lives forever." You rejoice with incomparable joy, O Virgin Theotokos, seeing your Son, who came forth from the womb as firstborn,

[?] now also rising as firstborn from the dead in divine glory, and first emptying the storehouses of Hades. In the law, the shadow and the letter… The corruption that once sprang from a tree you healed by a tree; and, shut within a tomb, you raised the dead in the tombs. You are the great and divine Pascha, O Word of the beginningless Father, who made mortals fellow citizens of the angels. Once the divine angel cried to the weeping women: "Take up joy and hasten to tell the apostles that the Master has risen and now goes before you into Galilee, as the Lover of mankind said before his passion." Rejoice, O earth; rejoice, [?]; leap for joy, you mortals: the Lord has risen, death is swallowed up; at last those held in bonds from all ages have been set free, celebrating with clapping the great, radiant and joyful Pascha. Your lament, O Pure One, has at last been turned into exultation; for behold, your Son, the Master of all and God, whom you saw on the cross without beauty, has risen in beauty and adorned all creation. She rejoices in you… Be glad, you heavens, and let all the earth exult; for today the Life of all rises from the dead. The Enemy is darkened by your shining forth, O Christ the Sun; and those who once sat in darkness have seen the light that never sets,

set free today from bondage to the spiritual Pharaoh. Let us keep God's holy Pascha in holiness. Be glad, pure Mother, as you behold the gladness of the universe, which has dispelled the gloom of Hades and refashioned mortals. The Church, seeing you lifted up… Hung on the tree like a vine, O Giver of life, you made the wine of salvation gush forth, gladdening all; therefore we cry to you: Glory to your power, O Lord. The gates of Hades opened to you in fear, O Savior; and its gatekeepers, seeing you clothed in the garment of vengeance, were astounded and shuddered, and from your face

The women who came with myrrh seeking you, the divine myrrh, [?] the one who announced your rising, O Savior, were struck with amazement. She who bore you, having seen you lifted up on the tree, O Word, [?] now rejoices as she beholds [?]; her we glorify as Theotokos. You, my Lord, came as light into the world… You, O Lord, who made man with your hands, stretched out your spotless hands upon the tree, and your side was pierced. You, O Lord, buried as one dead in the tomb, buried the malice of him who brought death upon the world, and raised up all. O holy, venerable and saving Pascha! O

divine [?] gladness, through you we who are of earth have been joined to the angels. You conceived Christ and bore him without corruption, O all-blameless one, him who destroyed the strength of Hades and saved mankind. I will sacrifice to you with a voice… I had been robbed by eating from the tree and had died through the Enemy's counsel, but you called me back when you were lifted up on the tree; and I had fallen into corruption, but with incorruption you [?]

Wrapped in a linen shroud, you were given over to burial; and, bursting the swaddling bands of Hades by divine might, you rose from the tomb as God, O Giver of life. O Lady truly so named, you bore the Lord of all, who destroyed the dominion of death and granted immortality and redemption to all mankind. In the furnace the children of Abraham… When the rocks of old saw the Rock of Life nailed to the wood of the cross, they split apart in great fear; the sun hid its light, and the foundations of the earth were shaken. To call back the fallen you lay down like a king in the tomb, with soldiers guarding you, O Lover of mankind. Blessed are you in the temple of your glory,

You snatched those who were fettered from the storehouses of Hades. O Word [?] by your all-working power, and [?] them crying out: Blessed are you. Seeing the Lord of life raised from the dead, O Maiden, you rejoice, and with the disciples you sing to him always: Blessed are you, O Lord. Stretching out his hands, Daniel… You raised your palms on the cross and shook the foundations of the earth; and those who had suffered the fall through a tree, O Master, you drew to yourself as they joyfully cried: Bless the Lord, all you works. They laid you dead in a pit, you who put death to death and gave life to those whom the author of evil had killed with his venomous bite, O only-begotten Word of God; therefore we cry to you: Bless the Lord. Pascha, the joyful day, has shone upon us, on which all of us who were held in bondage to the warring Enemy have received redemption; therefore we cry out: Bless the Lord, all you works. He who gave being to all has had you as the cause of his incarnation, and he came forth incorrupt from your incorrupt womb, he who breathes incorruption into the dead as they sing: Bless the Lord, all you works. The stone cut without hands from the mountain… I was wounded by the fruit of the tree through the counsel of Belial, but you, O Christ, wounded on the tree, have healed me; and becoming a curse for our sake, O Word, you set me free from the curse. "Why do you seek among the dead him who gives life to all things? Having destroyed the might of death, as he foretold, he has now risen," said the divine angel, flashing like lightning, to the myrrh-bearers. O most blessed Pascha, through which human nature has been carried over from earth

to the blessedness on high! O venerable and spotless Pascha, you are the redemption of the faithful. Hail, cause of joy; hail, destroyer of the curse; hail, glory of the Orthodox and refuge of those who sing your praises, O all-pure Mother of God, through whom we have been set free from corruption. Horse and rider… You who are wholly desire and wholly sweetness, O Jesus, tasted gall as you hung on the cross, plainly healing, O Master, the most bitter sin that had come upon me. Zion heard and was glad, as it is written, when you rose, O Word; for her daughters were the first to behold you and to receive the "Rejoice", being redeemed from the curse. Come, David, strike up the lyre, saying: Let us set forth a feast with shouts of joy; this is the day which the Master and Lord has made, the day of the resurrection. Hail, blessed one, full of divine grace; with you is the Master, who destroyed death and loosed mankind from the curse, O Lady, through your mediation, O Virgin Mother

…that I am God, who [?] flesh. On the tree you condemned sin, O Jesus, and [?] Hades when you were laid in the tomb; and you rose as God, raising with you the world, which glorifies your dominion. [?] Clap your hands, you nations, as the psalm says: the immortal God has risen, having emptied the palaces of death, and he reigns over all the earth as King of the universe. Saving Pascha, Pascha the recall of souls: this is the day of gladness and joy. Let us be glad in a mystical manner and glorify Christ, the God and Savior of all. Be glad, all-blameless and pure one, as you behold the Word, whom you made flesh, risen from the dead; and implore him to save from dangers and distress those who always honor you. He who established the earth upon nothing… The luminaries, seeing you, O Sun, willingly stretched out on the cross, drew in their light; all the earth quaked, the splendor of the temple was rent, the tombs were opened, and the dead rose from their graves. Joseph, wrapping you in fear in a spotless linen shroud, covers you in a tomb, O Word, you who always clothe the heaven with clouds, and who buried all the sin of our forefather, O Lover of mankind. Having rolled the stone away from the tomb, the divine angel cried to the women: "Why have you come with myrrh seeking him as a mortal? The Giver of life has risen; be filled with divine delight." All-blameless one, seeing Christ come forth from the tomb, like a bridegroom from the bridal chamber, wholly most beautiful, plainly

you took up joy and rejoiced together with the disciples, saying: The Lord has risen. Having perceived your divine self-emptying… On the tree you put the serpent to death; and, though counted among the dead, you who are free among the dead granted freedom to the prisoners there. The Lord has plainly become King; let all the earth exult. Death no longer rules, Hades no longer reigns; for it has vomited up those it held in bonds. O godly-minded women with myrrh, why do you seek Christ in the tomb as a mortal? He has risen, burying the stench of death, and has filled the faithful with fragrance. O spotless one, implore Christ, who came forth from your womb without in any way breaking the seals of virginity and rose in glory, to bring peace to the whole world. You who put on light like a garment… The God-slayers pierced your hands and your feet, O Savior, hanging you on the cross out of envy and giving you gall and vinegar to drink, O long-suffering one. How is Life laid in a tomb? How is he who gives breath to all mortals seen without breath, he who breathes life and redemption into the dead? The blessed Pascha, through which we have come up from the depths of the earth; Pascha, through which we were redeemed from bondage and carried over to the land of promise. Hail, you who knew not wedlock, all-blessed one, loosing of the curse, through whom the world has risen from its fall and glorifies the resurrection of the Giver of life. Raging with the surge… By being crucified, O my Jesus Christ, you opened paradise, which had been shut by disobedience; and by rising you raised all the faithful with you. They laid you in the lowest pit, voiceless and dead, you who breathe resurrection into the dead, O Giver of life, and gave life to those in Hades. Once an angel cried to the lamenting women: "Christ has risen; go and tell his apostles of his rising." "Rejoice," the Master says to you, O Virgin, as the cause of joy, when he rises from the tomb; implore him on behalf of all. The Lord, the supremely exalted God of our fathers… The incomprehensible one, having put on flesh, accepted the cross and destroyed death by death, willing to make the dead immortal. Pascha is the festival; let us all keep the feast. Christ has risen from the tomb on the third day, giving light to those who cry: O God, blessed are you. "Woman, why are you now bitterly overcome with tears?" Christ said near the tomb to the maiden as she sang: O God, blessed are you. She alone, before the other women, beheld you, O Christ, flashing forth in beauty from the tomb, the all-holy one, who alone heard the "Rejoice".

To you, the Maker of all… You, the Maker of all, hanging on the tree, the lawless enemies gave gall to drink — they who of old, thirsting in the wilderness, had sucked honey from the rock at your command, O Christ. You underwent death on the cross, O Christ, and, laid dead in the tomb for three days, you raise all those dead from all ages, who sing the praises of your love for mankind. Come, let us mystically clap our hands with a shout of joy to God, and sing: All you works, praise the Lord. You rejoice, O Pure One, seeing the Creator rising from the dead and bestowing grace and life on all, and freedom on those who confess him as God of all

Dance, Isaiah… Christ has risen, having destroyed the might of the Enemy. Be glad, you heavens; dance, O earth; death no longer reigns, for those whom it had bound by its wicked might have been taken from it at a divine command. The company of myrrh-bearing women hastened ahead to the tomb of Life, openly bringing myrrh to anoint you, the divine fragrance of all myrrh; but seeing you risen, it magnified you. Acceptable is the day which the Master and Lord has made, a glorious and most beautiful day; on it let us dance, crying out: O Master Christ, save your servants, who worship you in faith. You were made beautiful with the beauties of virginity, O spotless and pure one, when you bore the Maker of all and God, who despoiled Hades and bestows life on the dead, whose resurrection we celebrate with godly minds. Of old Moses prefigured your divine crucifixion, O Christ, when he lifted up the serpent; for by being crucified you opened to us the gates of paradise, and, laid as one dead in the tomb, you raised the dead with you and stripped Hades bare. Christ has risen! Let us sing, you peoples, and magnify his name; let us dance and chant faithfully to him as the victor over Hades, and cry out brightly: The Lord has risen; let us all keep the feast with joy. Let all the earth exult: Christ has risen, giving life to the dead; and appearing first to the myrrh-bearers, he cries to them, "Rejoice," and charges them: "Go now and eagerly [tell] my friends of my divine rising

Hail, dwelling-place of the Creator; hail, rational paradise of the Lord; hail, heaven and throne and tabernacle, in which the Maker dwelt; and, O Pure One, having despoiled the joyless tabernacle of Hades, he raised up those sleeping there

Being Lord of all and Creator God… You underwent crucifixion and reproaches willingly, O Christ, to take away the reproach of us all; and you went down into the tomb as a mortal, raising up those who had been corrupted. Glory to your almighty authority, O most merciful one.

Now the Lord has become King, having mightily cast down the bitter might of the tyrant, plainly despoiled the palaces of Hades, and led out those held in bonds from all ages, who cry: Glory, O Master, to your might

This, as David cries in the Psalms, is truly the light-filled day of Pascha, which the God of all has made. Let us dance in exultation with the heavenly ranks and glorify Christ. O Lady of all, since you bore the Creator of the universe, O full of divine grace, when you saw him raised from the tomb you were filled with divine joy, glorifying his majesty. The prophet, foreseeing… Let creation be clothed in brightness: the Lord has risen from the dead, and he has raised all creation with himself, emptying the belly and storehouses of Hades and of death by divine strength. Let us glorify him in faith and longing. O most holy Pascha, cleansing of the whole world, Word and Power of God, grant us to partake of you in purity, we who with a sincere mind devoutly glorify you always as risen from the dead on the third day. Of old the godly women, bringing myrrh with tears, clearly saw a bodiless angel sitting at the tomb, who cried to them: "Stop weeping bitterly, for Christ [?]" O Virgin, without knowing man, you bore the Lord, and remained a virgin after childbirth in an awesome manner; therefore all of us, the faithful, with one mind truly glorify you as the ever-incorrupt Theotokos. By the bond of love… Granting peace to all by your cross, O Lord, you went down into Hades and sent down light to those held fettered there, and raised them up with you by your rising on the third day. You who of old fashioned man from dust, O Master, went down into the dust of death and snatched from unbreakable bonds those dead from all ages, who glorify your might and dominion, O Most High. We who have been redeemed from the Egypt of error, let us keep in faith today the most radiant Pascha, and glorify Christ, risen on the third day, who has illumined the

The unquarried mountain, the lampstand and divine table, the holy ark, the all-golden jar of manna, the most exalted throne of the King: so we praise you in song, O Mother of God. The uttermost abyss of sins… Of old Isaac clearly prefigured your passion; for as a lamb, O God of all, you were willingly sacrificed for the complete redemption of the world. Hades was wounded when your side was wounded, O Master,

and it released those who were formerly bound, when it saw you come with your soul among those beneath the earth. A company of women brings you myrrh as to one who has died; but seeing you risen, it rejoiced with the holy apostles, glorifying you, O Lord. O all-holy one, who bore God, the Holy of Holies, seeing him die willingly and rise from the dead, you have been filled with gladness. The youths in Babylon… When the sun saw you hanging on the cross, O Sun, it was darkened; the earth was shaken, the rocks were split, and the dead rose from their tombs singing your praises. Conversing with those in Hades with your soul, O our God, you raise with you by your awesome rising the dead, who cry out: Blessed are you, O Lord, the

Let us, the faithful, clothe ourselves with the virtues as with garments, flashing like lightning on the day of Pascha, and cry out brightly: Blessed are you, O Lord God. Seeing the victor over death, your Son and our God, raised from the tomb, O Pure One, you cried out: Blessed are you, O Lord God.

The blessed ones who kept the ancestral laws… Willingly you are crucified, O supremely good one, and you lie breathless in a new tomb; yet you breathe life into the dead, O Master, being Life itself; and, rising, you raise with you the world, which sings the praises of your might and chants in fear: Praise the Lord,

When you went down into the lowest pit, O Lord, the whole of human nature was raised up and redeemed from its gloomy prison, praising in song your great compassion and your boundless power; and they sing in fear: Praise the Lord. Let us rejoice as we celebrate the divine and venerable Pascha, the saving Pascha, the blessed Pascha, and let us sing with thanksgiving a hymn of victory to our God, the Giver of life who makes us new, chanting together: Praise the Lord. Hail, raising up of the fallen; hail, loosing of the curse, O full of divine grace; hail, gate untraversed; hail, cloud of light; hail, you who bore for the world its saving joy; hail, untilled earth; hail, shelter of those who cry: Praise the Lord. Of the Master's hospitality and of the immortal… Lifted up on the tree, you dashed down the Enemy; you went down into Hades and raised up all who were held captive there, putting to death, O Word, the strength and might of death by your authority. Having risen, you had compassion on Zion, O Giver of life, appearing to the disciples over many days and staying with them; and you commanded them to proclaim you among the nations as God, and as Lord and Savior of all.

O Pascha, bringing gladness to all the faithful! O Word of God the Father, through whom all of us who glorify you with longing have been redeemed from corruption, make us sharers in your kingdom. Among women you were shown to be a virgin who gave birth to God; ever entreat him, pure one, before whom Hades and death cowered, that those who magnify you in faith may be redeemed from every kind of evil and danger. [?] your [?] toward earthly … By a tree you abolished the evil that came through a tree, and by your death you gave life to those who had died through a tree, O Pascha blameless and divine, Jesus, almighty Word of God. Come, let us all dance in gladness: Christ has risen, having truly emptied the gloomy kingdom of Hades and made resurrection gush forth for the dead. Coming to the tomb at dawn, the myrrh-bearers beheld angels flashing with brightness; and so, seized with fear, they were taught the Redeemer's [?]

Rejoice, blessed one, full of God's grace, sole beauty of the angels, help of mankind; rejoice, you who by your childbearing shut the gates of death. “You who in the beginning … the heavens.” You who stretched out the heavens willingly stretched out your palms upon the tree, O Saviour; and when you were laid dead in the tomb [?], O Master, you gave life to the dead, and by your venerable rising you raised all mortals together with you. As a most pure lamb you were willingly slain, O Christ, freely calling back the one who had wretchedly died through disobedience at the Enemy's counsel, and by your divine compassion making him a citizen of paradise. This is the day of feast and festival, on which all creation devoutly dances for joy, rejoices in spirit, keeps the feast and cries: You who dawned from the dead, venerable Pascha, O Lord, glory to you. We the faithful joyfully sing your praises, All-holy one, who bore the God of all, who made joy, incorruption and life shine forth for all from the tomb, and overthrew the might and dominion of the Destroyer. “You who did not leave the Father's bosom …” Hung willingly on the tree of the cross, Jesus, lover of mankind, you made a public example of all the principalities of the Destroyer, and made life gush forth for the world. Having pulled down the bronze gates of Hades and shattered the bonds of death, O Christ, you freed all the prisoners by your power, and rose on the third day, O Word. Clothed in the white of the virtues, let us dance at the radiant feast: Pascha great and saving, Pascha, the recall and life of the world and its redemption [?]

“O Lord my God, out of the night [?] dawn …” O Lord my God, who by the cross took Hades captive, I praise your crucifixion, I honour your resurrection, through which I was redeemed from corruption and enriched with incorruption. O Lord my God, who for three days were numbered among the dead, free me, O Christ, from the deadness of the passions, and by your goodness bring to life my soul that has been put to death. O Lord my God, who by appearing filled the [?women] with joy and spoke to them the word “Rejoice,” fill my afflicted heart with divine gladness. O Lord my God, who did not loosen the locks of virginity of the Maiden of God who bore you without knowing wedlock, by her holy intercessions loosen the bonds of my offences. “Sick and tossed on the swell of worldly cares …” Of old, O Saviour, Jonah prefigured your burial, dwelling uncorrupted for three days in the belly of the sea monster and glorifying you; for, shut in the lowest pit, O Word, you rose from the dead on the third day. Let all creation dance on the day of Pascha; for on it you, the Almighty, rose from the tomb, having destroyed death, and to those who had fallen asleep from all ages you granted divine redemption, O Christ. The myrrh-bearing maidens came in haste to the tomb at dawn, seeking to see the Giver of life; but they beheld an angel crying out to them: “The [?] has risen; weep no more.” He who was born without seed, O Maiden, from your incorrupt womb, when willingly laid in the tomb did not see corruption, immaculate one; but giving life to those who had been corrupted, he raised them with himself by divine power. “The youths in the fire-blazing furnace …” The people of the lawless Hebrews crucified you, the Lawgiver, forgetting your wonders, O Christ, the supremely exalted God of our fathers. With exultant soul let us dance today on the festal day of Pascha, and cry out: “O supremely exalted …” Blessed is the tomb that bodily received you, O Giver of riches, who by your rising on the third day enriched us who had become poor and had wretchedly died, O Word. The world calls you blessed, O Virgin, who bore the blessed Word, who made blessed those mortals who obey him, all-blameless Maiden, Mother of God. “Unburnt by fire, conversing on Sinai …” When the rocks saw the Rock of life lifted up above a rock at the Place of the Skull, they were split; and the sun, hiding its rays, put on darkness, crying: “All you works of the Lord, the Lord …”

The company of the apostles saw you come forth from the tomb most beautiful, like a bridegroom from his chamber, and, keeping the feast of Pascha together, they proclaimed it to the families of the nations, crying: “All you works of the Lord, the Lord …”

“Why do you seek the Giver of life with myrrh, as though he were mortal? He has risen, having emptied the palaces of Hades,” cried a holy angel to the women from the tomb, singing. The choir of myrrh-bearers, O Mother of God, dances with you today at the resurrection of your Son, and so does all creation, spiritual and visible, truly crying aloud. “Without experience of corruption, the conception …” Proclaim the good news, O creation, of Christ's rising, the whole world both visible and invisible; clap your hands and cry out with one voice: “The Lord has risen, having emptied the storehouses and the palaces of death.” This is the day of resurrection, which the Almighty alone has made; on it let us dance, seeing the fallen nature of humanity made immortal and clothed again in its first beauty. You who rose from the tomb on the third day, O Word, raise my soul, put to death by transgressions; give it life, and direct it to the paths of your divine commandments, that I may magnify your goodness as is due. On the day of Pascha let us dance joyfully, and let us cry brightly to the Virgin, “Rejoice”; for she became for us the source of salvation and of divine immortality, having conceived the God of all. “In the furnace the children of Israel …” Having undone the [?curse] by your cross, you were laid in a tomb, and as the mighty one, O Christ, you overthrew the most gloomy kingdom of Hades, and you rose, raising all creation with yourself; therefore we praise you to all the ages. When you went up on the cross, the sun was quenched; but when you went down to Hades, O lover of mankind, light shone on the souls who were in darkness, shepherded by bitter death; therefore we praise you to all the …

Loose me, O Christ, bound as I am with the chains of sins, and shine on me the divine radiance of repentance, O Saviour, who by your rising, O Christ, rescued mankind from eternal darkness — the rising whose praises we sing to all the …

You who carry in your arms Christ, who took a body from you, O Virgin, implore him to take me too into his embrace, who now wander along all the trackless ways of life and daily meet with countless falls through a careless will. “A figure of your pure childbirth …” The sun saw you crucified between thieves, O Word, Sun that never sets, and it was darkened; mountains, hills and sea were shaken; Hades trembled and released the prisoners it held, who sing your praises. You appeared like a great sun, O Saviour, setting beneath the earth but rising again from the dead never to set, and you shed your light abroad; we magnify you unceasingly. O Saviour Jesus, who destroyed death by your death and raised up all who were held there.

“[?] me from the lowest pit,” I cry to you, “redeeming me from deadly passions and from sin.” The myrrh-bearers came weeping to the tomb at dawn, and not finding you, they saw an angel in white sitting there and crying: “The Lord has risen; hurry to announce his rising to his disciples.” All creation trembles, O Lady, at the mystery of your childbearing, which surpasses understanding; for you bear God Emmanuel, who for our sake, all-blameless one, became man, and who destroyed the dominion of death by the cross.

“Before whom angels tremble …” All creation [?beholds] your passion, O good one: the sun is quenched as you set upon the cross, and those once shut up in darkness see a great light and sing your praises, O compassionate one. Hades trembled, O Christ, when it saw you come down to it with your soul [?], and it gave back the dead of all the ages, who sing the praises of your love for mankind. Risen from the tomb, O Christ, you were seen by the godly women who were bringing spices; and you transformed their lament, you who are the consolation of all forever. Seeing the God whom you bore [risen] from the dead, you were seen to be full of joy, Virgin Mary; implore him, then, pure one, to wipe away completely every grief from our hearts. “The light-bearing …” When the most right-minded thief saw you willingly placed on the tree, he cried, “Remember me, Jesus, when you come in your kingdom”; and he became a dweller in paradise, justified by true faith alone. Seeing you among the dead, O Saviour, Hades was put to death, and it gave back the dead it had long ago swallowed, who glorify, O Christ, your ineffable power, your [?] mercy, your great compassion; through it save us also, King of all. Women came bringing myrrh to the tomb, and seeing you, O Christ, raised from the dead, they were filled with great joy and announced to your apostles that you had risen from the tomb, raising the world with you.

“The dew-bearing furnace of a supernatural wonder …” You willingly accepted death, lifted up in the flesh on the tree; and seeing you, the sun was quenched and the splendour of the temple was torn, O Almighty; therefore we praise you, singing: “Let creation bless …” Those who of old sat in the shadow of death saw a never-setting radiance when you, O Lord, descended among them with your soul; and they were loosed from the eternal bonds, praising you greatly and saying: “Let creation bless …” Going to the tomb at dawn, the women saw a dazzling angel, who said: “The Redeemer has risen; why do you still count the living among the dead? Be filled with joy and cry aloud: ‘Let creation bless …’”

“A strange and wondrous mystery I behold …” Healing the pain of the first-formed man, you suffered pain, O Saviour, hanging willingly on the tree; and laid willingly in the tomb, you raised with yourself those who slept, who sing the praises of your awesome dispensation. When of old the band of apostles saw you risen, O Lord, they worshipped you with fear and joy; and you cried to them: “See, my words have come to pass; so do not be downcast, but rejoice.” Joseph the righteous wrapped you, O Saviour, in a linen shroud and lovingly laid you in a brand-new tomb; but you, having plainly shattered the gates and bars of Hades, raised the dead whom death had overpowered and swallowed before. The myrrh-bearers exulted on hearing of Christ's rising, and so they cried to the apostles: “Run quickly! See — do not grieve, but rejoice: the Lord of all has risen from the dead.” When you saw Christ risen from the bridal chamber of the tomb like a bridegroom, all radiant, incomparable in beauty, you were filled with joy, O Maiden; entreat him that those who sing your praises may be delivered from corruption and punishment. “This is the chosen and holy day …” Glory to Christ, who overthrew the Enemy and despoiled Hades by his descent into it, and gave life to the mortals whom it had overpowered and swallowed, who sing his praises to the ages. “See the place where he was laid who overthrew death and Hades by his power,” cried the one who appeared, flashing like lightning, to the myrrh-bearing women; “so do not seek Life among the dead.” Hades, meeting you below, O Word, was embittered, unable to come near you, and at your command it quickly gave back the dead it had swallowed, who praise your might with one voice. You saw risen from the dead, O Virgin, the Word whom you ineffably carried in the flesh, and your soul was filled with joy, as you sing the praises of his condescension to all the ages. “Shine, shine …” Though you are the Creator of hours and days, O Redeemer, on the sixth day and at the sixth hour you willingly endured, compassionate one, the shameful cross, to redeem us all and reconcile us, O Christ, to the Father. Groaning, Hades comes to meet you, O Redeemer, and swiftly sends away the prisoners it held, who with divine voices sing the praises, O Word, of your power that surpasses understanding and of your awesome condescension. Women came in haste with myrrh in the deep dawn to anoint your immaculate body, and an angel said to them: “The Author of life has risen; be filled with godly joy.”

When you saw the Light that shone on those sitting in the shadow of death [?rising] from the dead like the sun, O Virgin, you glorified him, dancing with all the myrrh-bearing women. “Make the radiant … dawn upon us …” The people of the Hebrews crucified you, the long-suffering Word, who by your crucifixion save a countless people and all the nations, O Christ our God, lover of mankind. At your resurrection you did not disturb the seals on the stone, just as at your birth you did not open the locks of virginity of her who bore you, O Christ our God. The women, beholding the bodiless one in a strange form, flashing with divine light, were struck with amazement and heard: “Do not weep; the Lord has risen.” Immaculate one, you have borne the holy Lord of hosts, Mother of God, who emptied the palaces of Hades and raised up with himself the lump of our human nature. “He who [saved] the hymn-singers in the furnace …” Christ, who was willingly crucified and laid in a tomb, and who abolished the might of death,

Risen, you said to the disciples: “Hasten to proclaim my power to the whole world, driving out the darkness of polytheism with the light of truth.” As higher than the heavens, loftier than the Cherubim and more honoured than all creation, all-holy Virgin, intercede for those who always glorify you in faith. “The life-receiving, ever-flowing spring …” Let all the earth exult today, and let the clouds rain down gladness: the Lord of glory, who was crucified, has risen, freeing us from the corruption of death and, in his compassion, making us radiant with incorruption. Once, to the holy women bringing myrrh with tears, the dazzling angel joyfully declared: “Why do you seek Life in the tomb among the dead? See, he has risen and enlightened all things.” The luminous rising of our God, shining brighter than the rays of the sun, enlightens the faithful in the Spirit through all the ages and guides them to salvation; let us celebrate it with a pure mind. O Mother of God, who bore eternal Life, give life to us who are dead in trespasses, and guide us to do what truly leads to life, that we may ever magnify you in faith. “The [?] of the fire …” Him who was [?lifted up] on the cross and buried in the flesh

willingly, and who shattered the iron gates and bars of Hades — the Lord who rose from the tomb on the third day — let us glorify. Let heaven exult, and let the earth be glad together with mankind: Christ has risen and appeared to his disciples, and eating with them he filled their hearts with [?joy]. To the weeping women the Giver of life proclaimed joy as they clasped his most holy feet, whose sound our foremother Eve had once feared within paradise. With most holy voices we glorify you, the Mother of God, as clearly holier than the ranks on high, and as the divine bridge that carries mortals over to the choirs beyond the world. “God the Word, from God …” O the folly of the Hebrews! How they unjustly condemn to death on the tree Christ, who alone is righteous and who, with divine sovereignty, breathes life into the dead in Hades! Honouring his divine resurrection, we sing its praises

While the seals were still in place, you rose from the [?tomb], O Christ, the resurrection of all, and you were made manifest to the disciples, teaching them the hidden mysteries and crying: “Go into the whole world, proclaiming my glory.” This all-holy day of the rising, the consolation of souls and joyful gladness, calls the faithful together to keep the feast in a godly way and to cry: Father, Son and divine Spirit, glory to you. Virgin who gave birth to the Light, by your intercessions illumine our thoughts and our hearts with your divine light, scattering the mist of the passions and making us all sharers in the day that knows no evening.

“Attend, my people, to the law …” You who made man with your hand, O Almighty, had your hands nailed to the tree, redeeming us from the hand of the Enemy. Striking the lightless prison of Hades, O Christ, you seized the prisoners it held and, as the mighty one, raised them with yourself. Seeing you, O Christ, risen from the tomb on the third day, the apostles worshipped you and proclaimed your rising everywhere. Groaning and shedding tears, the godly women reached the holy tomb, and were taught of Christ's resurrection. All-blameless Lady, you conceived the one who holds all things together, who shattered the gates of Hades and rose on the third day, as he had said. “Him who to Moses in the bush …” Lifted up on the cross, you lifted up the world with you; and laid in a tomb, O Saviour, you raise those who sleep in the tombs, who glorify your great compassion. Descending among the dead, you put Hades to death, and shattered the gates and bars of death, and

you lead out with might [?] those who were truly fettered, O salvation of all. You appeared to your disciples with many proofs over forty days, compassionate one, assuring them, so that they would proclaim to the whole world a God who had risen. You are the life of all; you, O Word, are the consolation of the dead and of the living, the joy and the illumination, who shone forth from a Virgin and rose from the tomb for the [?] of all

“Who among the earth-born has heard of such a thing?” You who were crucified rose from the dead on the third day, as you had foretold, raising the world with you by your resurrection; and you appeared first to the myrrh-bearing women, saying “Rejoice,” O joy of all who long for you with all their soul, most merciful one. Now corruption has been abolished: for Christ, incorruption and life, has risen from the dead and eats with his own apostles, teaching them higher and divine things and saying to them: “From Jerusalem do not —”

Once, to women bringing myrrh with tears, an angel said: “Why do you seek the living among the dead? Today he has risen, as he foretold; he is not here, for he has emptied the tombs and, as lover of mankind, has breathed immortality into the dead.” Seeing your Son and God risen from the dead, O Mother of God, you were filled with joy, you who are the cause of joy and gladness for all; therefore every soul joyfully sings your praises and glorifies you, ever-virgin. “The desert has blossomed like a lily, O Lord …” Seeing you suffer willingly on the tree, O Master, creation was changed and heaved like the sea, and the dead rose from their tombs. When all-devouring death saw you come into Hades with your soul, O Lord, Giver of life, it cowered and released the prisoners it had swallowed.
